title: One training step
summary: A training step clears old gradients, computes loss, finds new gradients and updates weights. Each step has a separate job.
introduction: A training step clears old gradients, computes loss, finds new gradients and updates weights. Each step has a separate job. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: A training step clears old gradients, computes loss, finds new gradients and updates weights. Each step has a separate job.

blocks.code:
import torch

model = torch.nn.Linear(1, 1)
optimizer = torch.optim.SGD(model.parameters(), lr=0.01)
x = torch.tensor([[1.], [2.]])
y = torch.tensor([[2.], [4.]])
optimizer.zero_grad()
loss = torch.nn.functional.mse_loss(model(x), y)
loss.backward()
optimizer.step()
print(loss.item() >= 0)
blocks.title: One training step

blocks.text: The check prints True because squared-error loss is nonnegative. One update is only a demonstration, not a trained reliable model.

blocks.text: Forgetting zero_grad can mix gradients from multiple steps unintentionally.
